transcript:
**Approach:** I added semantic deduplication to collapse entries expressing the same underlying constraint.

The solution has two parts:

1. **`extractConstraintCore()`** — analyzes entry text to identify its semantic category. Entries mentioning ops-related keywords (ops, operate, run, maintain, stateful, always-on, infrastructure, service) all map to a single category `"ops_burden"`. Entries that don't match any pattern return themselves unchanged (keeping domain-specific constraints distinct).

2. **`deduplicateEntries()`** — tracks which constraint cores have been seen, keeps only the first occurrence of each core, and discards later duplicates. This preserves the original wording of whichever statement came first while eliminating verbatim repeats.

3. **Integration** — the `project()` function now deduplicates each list (ruledOut, limits, warns) independently before rendering them.

**Why this works:** The five constraints you listed would all extract to `"ops_burden"`, so only the first one stays in the output. The deduplication is deterministic (depends on order in the record arrays, not on some external ML model), which fits the "Fold the record stream into the injected summary deterministically" commit message.
